quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights are ordered with red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that other vehicles will be entering your lane from the right. Be prepared to let them merge safely.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but don't see an opening in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for an opening.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for an opening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for an opening.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a safe gap in traffic. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you need room to speed up and match traffic flow before entering the freeway.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you there is a steep hill coming. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to avoid brake damage.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatal crash.
You need more following distance at higher speeds.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases. Higher speeds also mean longer stopping distances, so you need more space between your vehicle and others.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to a steep hill. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the right lane is ending. Prepare for merging traffic coming from the right.

questions.question: Slow vehicles should use the left-hand lane, except when passing or making a left turn.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Slow vehicles must use the right-hand lane, except when passing or making a left turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction the arrow points.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to have complete control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and easy to miss, so be extra careful around them.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when you pull next to a curb and when you pull away from it.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you check for a gap, match the traffic speed, and signal. What should you do next?

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait until the lane is completely clear before merging.

questions.explanation: Merge smoothly into the gap when it is safe. Do not expect other drivers to make space for you. Stay alert and watch for other vehicles.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you cannot see.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: Leave a note attached to the car with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: This sign warns that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right only.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves to the right and then curves to the left.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly without sudden movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly without sudden movements.
questions.explanation: Avoid hard braking and sharp turns in bad weather. These sudden movements make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Frequently to see traffic behind you.
Only to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently to see traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often while driving. This helps you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same traffic rules.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than cars.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely is dangerous because you may not have enough time to stop if the motorcycle stops suddenly.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before trying to stop or turn.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street to another one-way street, start from which lane?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start the turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead makes an extreme change in direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes an extreme change in direction.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign tells you to slow down and prepare for a sharp turn.

questions.question: When driving at night on a poorly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: Can you turn right at a red light after stopping and yielding?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You can turn right at a red light if there is no sign prohibiting it. You must stop completely and yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway through the exit lane.
As you approach the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is beginning.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway starts ahead. Keep to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop and watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Drive carefully through and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at construction zones. Staring slows traffic and causes congestion. Keep your eyes on the road and drive carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can drive in either direction in this lane.
Traffic moves in both directions.
You are coming to a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic travels in both directions on this road.

questions.question: Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights from sunset to sunrise.

questions.question: Taillights do not need to be on after dark.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise. You also need two red taillights that can be seen from 500 feet away. Motorcycles and mopeds need only one taillight.

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
The vehicle is moving slowly.
There is work ahead on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road work vehicles, and carts pulled by animals.
